A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConfiG research work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables and figures, and support reliable comparison despite substantial methodological and experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and distillation experiments on CelebA, SpuCo Birds and Spurious ImageNet, together with quantitative ablations and qualitative augmentation examples.

after.justification: v3 reports original experiments on CelebA-HQ, SpuCo Birds, BAR and ImageNet-100, plus Oxford Pets experiments and extensive appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes generation from original-class latent optimization to inter-class prompt-to-prompt initialization followed by optimization toward a different target class. Equation 7 changes from maximizing teacher confidence plus transformed student uncertainty to minimizing student confidence plus transformed teacher uncertainty, jointly optimizing latent, null-text and conditioning. Appendix E also introduces a Hyper-SD variant using IP-Adapter guidance.

E1.justification: v3 adds BAR activity classification under place shift and five-shot Oxford Pets evaluation without deliberately imposed covariate shift (Appendix L). It also substitutes CelebA-HQ for CelebA while retaining bird and ImageNet classification. These changes substantially broaden the represented tasks and evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Diff-Mix and Diff-II join the evaluated diffusion baselines in v3 Tables 2–3. The TAB combination experiments in v1 are replaced by LfF and uLA comparisons in v3 Table 8; plain Stable Diffusion and CutMixPick evaluations disappear. GIF, DistDiff, DA-Fusion and ActGen remain, with DA-Fusion's spelling change not treated as a new method.

E3.justification: Training changes from 100 epochs with cosine decay and validation-selected checkpoints to 300 epochs with constant learning rates and final-checkpoint evaluation. Main generation budgets become approximately FLOP-matched rather than equal augmentation counts. SpuCo Birds switches from a specially fine-tuned ViT-B teacher to zero-shot CLIP with species aggregation. CelebA-HQ uses reversed official split roles and eight groups rather than sixteen; ImageNet training changes to 100 spurious-feature-selected images per class.

E4.justification: v3 adds component-isolation, weaker-teacher, replacement-probability, target-class and single-step-generator studies, together with explicit failure cases and no-shift evaluation. ConvNeXt experiments replace the TinyViT/ResNet studies, and the ERM-plus-EDRM loss ablation is removed. Existing augmentation-count, stronger-augmentation and synthetic-sample difficulty analyses are revised rather than simply added anew.

E5.justification: Reported group-shift results change from means and standard deviations over three trainings in v1 Table 1 to six in v3 Table 2. Appendix B additionally states that synthetic datasets are generated once and ImageNet training is performed once per method. The uncertainty-reporting framework otherwise remains mean plus standard deviation, without new confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Core results are replaced under revised conditions: ConfiG's ViT-T ImageNet accuracy is 93.3% in v1 Table 2 and 80.02% in v3 Table 3, which is not a same-setting performance decline. Substantial new results include BAR, where ConfiG's mean SMA is 58.66% versus Diff-Mix's 59.28%, and Oxford Pets, where ConfiG trails both evaluated baselines at the smaller augmentation budget.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix A replaces v1's infinity-norm approximation assumptions with a KL-divergence teacher bound and explicit risk-gap assumptions. Proposition 1 revises the mixing-rate constraint and changes the final bound from min{Ω−Θ, Ω/2} to max{Ω−αΘ, Ω/2}. The lemma and proof are rewritten, and a new derivation connects teacher-label concentration and confidence separation to the required risk gap.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains confidence-guided augmentation for distillation under unknown covariate shift. However, v1's blanket superiority claim is qualified in v3's abstract and conclusion to best or second-best sample mean accuracy, while the claimed evaluation scope expands to BAR and CelebA-HQ.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limitations concerning estimation of the theoretical constants and augmentation distribution, applicability to location-sensitive tasks, and failures caused by unnatural generation or stalled optimization. It proposes domain mismatch as an explanation for weaker Hyper-SD results. The earlier two-augmentation optimum is replaced by dataset-dependent scaling conclusions, and the teacher-dependence discussion is revised around the new teacher setup and weaker-teacher experiments.

D1.justification: Appendices B, C and N greatly expand reproducibility information: inversion and denoising settings, separate optimization learning rates, stopping rules, background regularization, Hyper-SD/IP-Adapter configuration, checkpoint references, teacher-logit aggregation and baseline-specific parameters. FLOP measurement assumptions and generation multipliers are documented. Conversely, v1's V100 generation-time measurements are no longer reported.

R1.justification: The cited literature substantially expands around inter-class augmentation, prompt-to-prompt editing, consistency models, Hyper-SD, IP-Adapter and newer augmentation and robustness research. Diff-Mix becomes explicit motivation for a method component, while additional discussion positions ConfiG relative to fast diffusion and context-guided generation. These are substantive additions beyond citation renumbering or publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The method exposition is reorganized into named discussions of empirical motivation, latent optimization, inter-class mixing and the auxiliary student. Experimental and limitations prose is extensively rewritten, and implementation material is consolidated into Appendix B. The former A.1–A.13 appendix structure is substantially reordered into topical Appendices A–O, with some analyses moved out of the main text.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a different document template and extensively redesigns tables and figures. The large ERM/EDRM comparison table becomes separate comparison and ablation tables; v1's combined Table 2 is separated into ImageNet results and appendix diagnostics. Qualitative panels now emphasize inter-class mixing stages, with new failure-case and generator-variant displays, additional diagnostic plots and revised legends and captions.

improvement.justification: v3 repairs the unsupported final bound in v1's Proposition 1 and explicitly limits the theory's practical interpretation. It replaces the specially fine-tuned bird teacher, which v1 acknowledged was impractical, with a zero-shot procedure, strengthens component and applicability testing, and documents systematic approximate compute matching. Failure cases and unfavorable Oxford Pets results provide useful boundaries. Although some earlier ablations are lost and changed settings prevent direct performance comparisons, the gains in mathematical soundness, experimental scrutiny and reproducibility substantially improve the paper.
